questions.text: What is the Internet?
options: A company that sells phones, tablets and computers
A program used to visit websites and read pages
A huge network that connects computers and other devices around the world
One very large computer that stores every website

questions.text: Which of these can connect to the Internet?
options: A ruler
A paper book
A smart TV
A pencil

questions.text: What is the difference between the Internet and Wi-Fi?
options: The Internet is the worldwide network; Wi-Fi is a way to connect to a network without a cable
The Internet is a cable in your home; Wi-Fi is the company that sells it
They are exactly the same thing, so either word can be used for either
The Internet is a Wi-Fi router; Wi-Fi is a website you visit with a browser

questions.text: What is a network?
options: A group of connected devices
A program used to open websites
A collection of related web pages
A secret word that protects your account

questions.text: What is a website?
options: A device that connects your phone to the Internet
A program used to visit and view websites online
A collection of related web pages available on the Internet
One single page that you can read in a browser

questions.text: What is a web page?
options: A company that provides Internet access to homes
One page that you can view in a web browser
A whole collection of websites on the Internet
A cable that connects a computer to a router

questions.text: What is a web browser?
options: A company that gives Internet access
A website that stores emails
A program used to access websites
A device that connects to Wi-Fi

questions.text: Which of these is a web browser?
options: Google Search
DuckDuckGo
Mozilla Firefox
Bing

questions.text: What does a search engine do?
options: Helps you find information on the Internet
Connects your phone to a Wi-Fi network
Stores all the files that you create online
Sends and receives your email messages

questions.text: Which of these is a search engine?
options: Safari
Bing
Microsoft Edge
Google Chrome

questions.text: Which sentence is correct?
options: Chrome and Google are both routers
Chrome and Google are both websites you cannot open
Chrome is a search engine and Google is a browser
Chrome is a browser and Google is a search engine

questions.text: What is a URL?
options: A program that finds information for you online
The address of a page or resource on the Internet
A company that provides Internet access to schools
A device that connects your home to the ISP

questions.text: What is a link?
options: A message that you send to another person by email
A cable that joins two computers in a network
A secret word that protects your online account
Something you can click to go to another page or website

questions.text: What is a server?
options: A computer that provides information or services to other computers
A company that sells phones and mobile data plans
A device that connects your home to the ISP
A program that lets you visit websites and pages

questions.text: What does ISP stand for?
options: Internet Safety Program
Internet Service Provider
Internal Server Path
International Search Page

questions.text: What is a router?
options: A company that provides Internet access to homes
A computer that stores websites for other people
A program that helps you find pages on the web
A device that helps connect devices to a network

questions.text: What does a phone usually need to use mobile data?
options: Only a Wi-Fi password and a wireless router at home
An Ethernet cable connected to a desktop computer
A SIM card or eSIM, a mobile network signal and a data plan
A printer and a memory card for storing pictures

questions.text: You turn off Wi-Fi on your phone and browse using your SIM card. Which connection are you using?
options: Ethernet
Bluetooth only
Wi-Fi
Mobile data

questions.text: Which type of connection uses a physical cable?
options: Bluetooth
Wi-Fi
Mobile data
Ethernet

questions.text: Which of these is a risk of the Internet?
options: Finding learning materials
Cyberbullying
Selling products online
Communicating across countries

questions.text: Can we trust everything we read online?
options: Yes, if the page has pictures and videos on it
No, because anyone can publish information online
Yes, if the information is on a website page
Yes, because computers never make any mistakes

questions.text: Before believing information online, which question should you ask?
options: Is the page very long?
Who wrote it?
How many colours does the page have?
How many links are on the page?

questions.text: Why should you check when a web page was published?
options: The date changes the address of the page online
Old pages are always false and should be deleted
Newer pages always load much faster than old ones
Information can become old and out of date

questions.text: Why should you check more than one source?
options: Because one website is never able to open on its own
Because using more sources saves your mobile data
If reliable sources agree, you have stronger evidence
Because different sources always give different facts

questions.text: What is clickbait?
options: A tool that protects your computer from viruses
A search engine that finds pictures and videos
A type of email that comes from a teacher
Content designed mainly to make people click

questions.text: When using an online map, what should you NOT do?
options: Search for a school near your home town
Search for the city of Kigali in Rwanda
Share your home address publicly
Look for a park or a hospital in the area

questions.text: What is email?
options: A way of sending and receiving messages using the Internet
A search engine that finds information for you
A web browser used to open websites and pages
A cable that connects two computers together

questions.text: Which of these is an email address?
options: https://student
student.gmail
www.student.com
student@gmail.com

questions.text: What goes in the To field of an email?
options: The email address of the person who should receive it
The password that protects your email account
The size of the file that you are attaching
The name of the browser that you are using

questions.text: What is the Subject of an email for?
options: It is where you type the address of the sender
It tells the receiver what the email is about
It is where you attach a picture or document
It is where you write the password for the account

questions.text: What happens if you type the wrong email address?
options: Your message may go to the wrong person
The email fixes the address by itself
Nothing can go wrong
The email is always deleted

questions.text: What is an email attachment?
options: A file included with an email
The short line that says what it is about
A reply that you send to a message
A folder that keeps deleted messages

questions.text: What does Compose mean in Gmail?
options: Signing out
Deleting an email
Replying to an email
Creating a new email

questions.text: What is the email safety rule about passwords?
options: Write your password on the class board
Send your password to teachers by email
Share your password with friends you trust
Your password is a secret, not a message

questions.text: Google says you are too young to create an account. What should you do?
options: Enter a different age
Stop and ask your teacher or parent for help
Use a stranger's phone number
Ask a friend to make one for you in secret

questions.text: What is phishing?
options: An attempt to trick you into giving away information or doing something unsafe
A very fast Internet connection that is provided by an ISP company
A safe way of downloading music, videos and pictures from a website
A special search engine used by teachers to find lesson plans

questions.text: Which is a warning sign of a suspicious email?
options: It uses your correct name and the correct school address
It is polite and comes from your teacher, who you know well
It tells you about today's homework on the school platform
It demands immediate action, such as clicking a link right now

questions.text: You get an email saying you won 5,000 dollars if you enter your Gmail password. What should you do?
options: Forward it to all your friends so that they win too
Do not click or reply, and show it to a teacher or trusted adult
Reply with your phone number so that they can call you
Enter your password quickly so that you get the prize

questions.text: You receive an unexpected attachment called Congratulations!!!.exe from someone you do not know. What should you do?
options: Open it to see what it is
Download it and share it
Reply and ask them to send more
Do not open it

questions.text: What is a file?
options: A device that connects to Wi-Fi
A program that finds web pages
A cable that joins two computers
Information stored digitally

questions.text: What does download mean?
options: Receiving information from the Internet and saving it to your device
Sending a file from your device to an online service
Turning off the Wi-Fi on your phone or tablet
Deleting a file that you no longer need on your computer

questions.text: What does upload mean?
options: Reading a web page in your browser window
Printing a document on the school printer
Receiving a file from the Internet and saving it on your device
Sending a file from your device to an online service

questions.text: A stranger tells you to download a file that asks you to turn off your computer's security. What should you do?
options: Do not download it, and ask a trusted adult
Share the file with friends so they can try it
Download it quickly before the link stops working
Turn off security and then download it anyway

questions.text: Online messages should be:
options: Written in capital letters so they look important
Rude but short, so that people notice them
Clear, polite, respectful and appropriate
Sent to strangers so that you make more friends

questions.text: During an online meeting, what should you do when you are not speaking?
options: Share the meeting link publicly
Make noises
Mute yourself
Interrupt others

questions.text: Which of these should you NOT share with strangers online?
options: Your favourite sport
Your favourite colour
Your favourite animal
Your home address

questions.text: Which password is the strongest?
options: Your first name written with a capital letter at the start
The word password followed by your birth year
A mixture of small and capital letters, numbers and special characters
The numbers 1234 because they are easy to remember

questions.text: Which of these should you never announce publicly online?
options: My favourite colour is blue
I like football
I am learning to use Word
I am home alone

questions.text: What is cyberbullying?
options: Bullying that happens using digital technology
A very fast Internet connection at home or school
A kind of virus that spreads between computers
A type of game that people play with friends online

questions.text: Someone is bullying you online. What should you do?
options: Bully them back so that they learn how it feels to be hurt
Share your password with them so that they stop the messages
Do not respond with more bullying, block or report them, and tell a trusted adult
Delete your account and do not tell any adult about it

questions.text: What is Artificial Intelligence (AI)?
options: A type of cable that connects a computer to a router in the home
Technology that allows computers to perform tasks that normally need human-like abilities
A kind of website address that ends with the letters AI in the URL
A special type of Wi-Fi network that works faster than a normal connection

questions.text: AI can make mistakes. What should you do with important information from an AI?
options: Always check it
Send it to your friends without checking
Always believe it
Ignore all AI answers

questions.text: What is a prompt?
options: A virus that spreads between computers
A kind of password that protects your account
A type of website that shows pictures
The instruction or question you give to an AI

questions.text: Which is the best prompt?
options: Lions lions lions lions lions lions
Give me five interesting facts about lions for a 10-year-old
Write my whole lion homework so I can copy it
Tell me some things about animals in general

questions.text: Which of these should you never give an AI?
options: A request for quiz questions
Your password
A request to explain photosynthesis
A question about the sky

questions.text: An AI says the largest planet is Earth. What is the best thing to do?
options: Check with reliable sources, because AI is a helper and not the only source of truth
Believe it, because AI is always right about every single fact that it gives
Copy it straight into your homework, because it sounds so confident and sure
Ask the AI to say it again and then stop checking, because it repeated it

questions.text: Which is a good way to use AI for schoolwork?
options: Ask it to explain a difficult idea or create quiz questions to practise
Share your password with it so that it can log in to your accounts
Ask it to do all of your homework so that you do not have to learn
Copy its answers word for word and say that you wrote them yourself
